St. Martin's Day Spiced Biscuits

Served at: St. Martin's Day (Martinstag)

Makes about 3 dozen cookiesPrep 30 min (plus 1 hour chilling)Cook 10-12 min

These warmly spiced biscuits are a delightful treat for St. Martin's Day, celebrated on November 11th. Marking the end of the harvest season and a time for sharing, these comforting cookies are perfect for enjoying after a lantern parade or with a warm drink at family gatherings. Their aromatic spices evoke the cozy spirit of autumn and the approaching winter holidays.

Ingredients

  • 2 1/2 cups (300g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1 cup (226g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 1 cup (200g) packed light brown sugar
  • 1 large egg
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract

Method

  1. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, ginger, cloves, nutmeg, and salt; set aside.
  2. In a large bowl, using an electric mixer, cream together the softened butter and brown sugar until light and fluffy, about 2-3 minutes.
  3. Beat in the egg and vanilla extract until well combined.
  4. Gradually add the dry ingredient mixture to the wet ingredients, mixing on low speed until just combined and a soft dough forms.
  5. Divide the dough in half, flatten each half into a disk, wrap tightly in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour (or up to 2 days).
  6. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C) and line baking sheets with parchment paper.
  7. On a lightly floured surface, roll out one disk of dough to about 1/4-inch (6mm) thickness.
  8. Use cookie cutters (stars, moons, or simple rounds are traditional) to cut out shapes and carefully transfer them to the prepared baking sheets, leaving about 1 inch (2.5 cm) between cookies.
  9. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden.
  10. Let the cookies cool on the baking sheets for 5 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.

Tips

  • For extra festive flair, dust cooled cookies with powdered sugar or drizzle with a simple glaze made from powdered sugar and a touch of milk.
  • The dough can be made ahead of time and stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 days, or frozen for up to 1 month.
  • Adjust the spice levels to your preference; a pinch of cardamom can also be a lovely addition.
